Perfect, that gives me a clear structure.

**Week 1 (heat wave, min days Wed to Fri)**
- Wed/Thu/Fri, 1:30 to 2:30 pm: lunch check for your grandma if your dad is working, then a short break. Heat makes afternoons drag, so stay inside.
- 2:30 to 4:00 pm: AP Calc problem set, the hardest one first. Use the school laptop.
- After dinner and dishes, 7:30 to 8:30 pm: AP Chem reading for Mr. Ostrowski's class, about 20 pages or one section a night, with 5 lines of notes each.
- 10:30 to 11:30 pm: essay brainstorming on the desktop, Wed and Fri only. Freewrite, no editing.
- Lights out by 12:30 at the latest on Thu so you aren't wrecked Friday.
- Saturday: 1 to 2 hours total of APUSH and AP Lang catch-up, leaving the rest free.

**Week 2 (regular schedule)**
- Mon/Wed: Calc problem sets right after school, about 90 minutes.
- Tue/Thu: Chem reading, 45 minutes after dishes.
- Mon/Thu 10 to 11 pm: essay drafting on the desktop, capped at an hour.
- Physics and APUSH: 30 minutes each, rotating on the open evenings.
- One light night with nothing scheduled.

The essay slots sit late because that's when you have the desktop, and I capped them at an hour so they don't push your bedtime later. Want this as a checklist you can tick off?
